facts.statement: Lourinhasaurus was a herbivorous sauropod dinosaur that lived in the Late Jurassic of Portugal.
facts.quote: Lourinhasaurus is an extinct genus of herbivorous sauropod dinosaur dating from Late Jurassic strata of Estremadura, Portugal.

facts.statement: The type specimen of Lourinhasaurus was discovered in June 1949 by American geologist Harold Weston Robbins near Alenquer.
facts.quote: In June 1949 a partial skeleton of a large sauropod, found by American geologist Harold Weston Robbins, was excavated in a locality near Alenquer.

facts.statement: Pedro Dantas and colleagues proposed the new genus name Lourinhasaurus in 1998 based on a specimen from Porto Dinheiro.
facts.quote: In 1998, Pedro Dantas and colleagues publish their work on the Porto Dinheiro specimen, that they interpreted as being the same species as the Moinho do Carmo specimen. They proposed the combinatio nova Lourinhasaurus alenquerensis, and emended the diagnosis for the taxon, although mostly based on the Porto Dinheiro specimen.

facts.statement: The Moinho do Carmo specimen was designated the lectotype for Lourinhasaurus alenquerensis in 2003.
facts.quote: It was not until 2003 that the Moinho do Carmo specimen was appointed as the lectotype for Lourinhasaurus alenquerensis.

facts.statement: A complete re-description and phylogenetic revision of Lourinhasaurus was published by Mocho and colleagues in 2014.
facts.quote: In 2014, Mocho and colleagues published a complete re-description of the Moinho do Carmo specimen, including elements never described before, and also provided a phylogenetic revision of Lourinhasaurus.

facts.statement: Lourinhasaurus lived approximately 150 to 145 million years ago during the Late Jurassic, spanning the Kimmeridgian to Tithonian stages.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente 150 y 145 millones de años entre el Kimmeridgiense y el Titoniense, en lo que es hoy Europa.

facts.statement: Lourinhasaurus is estimated to have reached 15 to 18 meters in length and weighed around 5 metric tons.
facts.quote: Lourinhasaurus alenquerensis has been estimated at 15-18 m in length and weighed around 5 MT.

facts.statement: The femur of Lourinhasaurus is estimated to be 1.68 meters long.
facts.quote: The femur of Lourinhasaurus is estimated at 1.68 m in length.

facts.statement: Lourinhasaurus was a heavy-bodied herbivore with a long neck, reaching about 17 meters in length.
facts.quote: Lourinhasaurus llegaba a medir cerca de 17 metros de largo, siendo un herbívoro de cuello largo de constitución pesada.

facts.statement: The first seven dorsal vertebrae had relatively high and bifurcated neural spines, while posterior dorsal vertebrae featured prominent longitudinal keels in their centers.
facts.quote: Se caracterizaba por la morfología de las primeras siete vértebras dorsales con apófisis neurales relativamente altas y bifurcadas, también las dorsales posteriores poseen quillas longitudinales ventrales prominentes en su centro.

facts.statement: Lourinhasaurus likely resembled Camarasaurus but had proportionally longer forelimbs.
facts.quote: Se cree que puede haberse parecido a Camarasaurus , aunque con extremidades anteriores proporcionalmente más largas.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis suggests Lourinhasaurus is a basal Macronarian closely related to Camarasaurus.
facts.quote: The phylogenetic hypotheses proposed by that work suggest that Lourinhasaurus is a basal member of the Macronaria closely related to Camarasaurus, in agreement with McIntosh's earlier views.

facts.statement: Lourinhasaurus is classified within the family Camarasauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Camarasauridae

facts.statement: The classification of Lourinhasaurus has been controversial, with some specimens originally referred to it later reinterpreted as belonging to other genera like Dinheirosaurus.
facts.quote: The research history of Lourinhasaurus is not without controversies, with referred specimens later being interpreted as not belonging to the genus (such as the type specimen of Supersaurus (=Dinheirosaurus) lourinhanensis).

facts.statement: The Porto Dinheiro specimen, initially used to define Lourinhasaurus, was later reinterpreted as a diplodocid named Dinheirosaurus lourinhanensis.
facts.quote: Just a year later, however, the Porto Dinheiro specimen was reinterpreted as a diplodocid, and given the new name Dinheirosaurus lourinhanensis.

facts.statement: The name Lourinhasaurus means "lizard from Lourinhã," even though the type specimen was not found in that municipality.
facts.quote: Lourinhasaurus means "lizard from Lourinhã" literally translated, despite the fact that the type specimen wasn't found in the Lourinhã municipality.

facts.statement: The first fossil remains were discovered in 1949 by Harold Weston Robbins near Alenquer.
facts.quote: El primer hallazgo se realizó en 1949 por Harold Weston Robbins , un esqueleto fósil parcial encontrado cerca de Alenquer

facts.statement: In 1957, Albert-Félix de Lapparent and Georges Zbyszewski named the species Apatosaurus alenquerensis.
facts.quote: fue en 1957 llamado Apatosaurus alenquerensis por Albert-Félix de Lapparent y Georges Zbyszewski

facts.statement: A second partial skeleton containing a tooth and one hundred gastroliths was found in 1983 near the city of Lourinhã.
facts.quote: El hallazgo de otro esqueleto parcial, ML 414, que incluye un diente y cien gastrolitos, en estratos de similar edad cerca de la ciudad de Lourinhã en 1983

facts.statement: Pedro Dantas and colleagues proposed in 1998 that the taxon represented a distinct form from Apatosaurus and Camarasaurus.
facts.quote: indujo a Pedro Dantas y colaboradores en 1998 a ver el taxón como una forma distinta de Apatosaurus y Camarasaurus

facts.statement: Based on the new evidence, Dantas and colleagues proposed the new genus Lourinhasaurus.
facts.quote: Por lo tanto, propusieron el nuevo género Lourinhasaurus

facts.statement: The genus name Lourinhasaurus refers to the location of the second skeleton found.
facts.quote: El nombre del género se refiere a la localidad del segundo esqueleto

facts.statement: In 1999, the second specimen was assigned its own genus name, Dinheirosaurus.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, ya en 1999 este segundo espécimen recibió un nombre de género propio, Dinheirosaurus

facts.statement: In 2003, Miguel Antunes and Octávio Mateus selected specific specimens as lectotypes for the species.
facts.quote: En 2003, Miguel Antunes en Octávio Mateus eligió los especímenes MIGM 4956-7, MIGM 4970, MIGM 4975, MIGM 4979-80, 4983-4 y MIGM 5780-1 como lectotipos

facts.statement: Lourinhasaurus alenquerensis is a member of the Eusauropoda.
facts.quote: Lourinhasaurus alenquerensis es miembro del Eusauropoda

facts.statement: The dinosaur was originally classified as a diplodocid.
facts.quote: Originalmente fue visto como un diplodócido

facts.statement: In 2004, Upchurch determined that the species was more basal and a sister taxon to Neosauropoda.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, Upchurch en 2004 descubrió que era más basal, un taxón hermano del Neosauropoda

facts.statement: A 2014 study by Mocho et al. suggested that Lourinhasaurus is a basal member of Macronaria and a type of Camarasauromorpha.
facts.quote: La hipótesis filogenética propuesta por Mocho et al. en 2014 sugiere que Lourinhasaurus es un miembro basal de Macronaria, una especie de Camarasauromorpha

facts.statement: The parent group for Lourinhasaurus is Camarasauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Camarasauridae

facts.statement: Lourinhasaurus belongs to the family Camarasauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Camarasauridae

facts.statement: Lourinhasaurus is classified in the class Saurischia.
facts.quote: Class: Saurischia

facts.statement: Lourinhasaurus lived during the Kimmeridgian to Tithonian stages, from 152.21 to 145.06 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Tithonian (152.21 to 145.06 million years ago)

facts.statement: The original material consisted of syntypes from the Sobral Member of the Lourinhã Formation.
facts.quote: El material originalmente consistía en una serie de sintipos del Miembro Sobral de la Formación Lourinhã

facts.statement: The fossil material consists of disarticulated bones from a single individual.
facts.quote: Consisten en huesos desarticulados de un solo individuo

facts.statement: It is debated whether the second specimen should be classified as Lourinhasaurus or the separate genus Dinheirosaurus.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, ya en 1999 este segundo espécimen recibió un nombre de género propio, Dinheirosaurus
